title: EXP-118 - Hello World Part 8 Phase 2 Runtime Check: FX_CustomerPortal in the Web Client, Customer ID 1 and One ButtonSignIn2 Click, Observing GridItems' FX_ItemsTile Tiles, Closed Without Saving
objective: Check at runtime what the Phase 2 Designer work (EXP-117) does (tutorial 04:32-04:47): open the User-scope Form FX_CustomerPortal in the Web Client, record its initial state (especially the GridItems band), type 1 in the Customer ID edit (EditCustID, unbound, EXP-111), click the sign-in page button ButtonSignIn2 once (Primary event FX_SignInBtn, Collection Refresh of 'secondary collection 2'), and record whether GridItems shows FX_Items records as FX_ItemsTile tiles (picture, item, description, cost). This also answers whether the handler's `object2` reaches the FX_Items collection. Then close the runtime Form without saving. Read-only with respect to data and metadata: no Save anywhere, no Designer change. The sign-in is a UI demonstration, not authentication (Part 8 instruction 4). Findings are observed only.

in_scope: Before browser interaction read AGENTS.md (the repository file, at the start of every task), docs/mongoose/transcripts/hello-world-pt8.md 'Instructions for AI agents' (lines 12-22), Phase 2 (lines 114-123) and transcript lines 362-364 (04:32-04:47), recipes/session/session-expiry-and-stale-designer.md, and only the final Outcome (operator) sections of the EXP-117, EXP-116, EXP-111 and EXP-095 records. Read nothing else. In a continuation task, AGENTS.md and the current task's part of this record are enough.
Create or update only experiments/EXP-118-hello-world-part-8-phase-2-runtime-sign-in-tiles.md and evidence/EXP-118/ documentation and evidence files.
Record the worker-written-file inventory and a cumulative browser action audit with exact counts.

Use the existing authenticated session without refresh, restart or configuration change. If a session expiry, logout card or sign-in page appears, record it and stop for the operator (EXP-107: the operator signs in manually); do not navigate, type credentials or screenshot a filled sign-in form. List the browser tabs before the first tab selection. Answer any prompt within the same task; never leave a prompt, dialog, menu or unsaved change open across tasks. After any pause, inspect the state read-only before acting and never replay an earlier action. Signed-out session (EXP-116): a server-event error together with a portal tab reading 'Logout Successful' means the session ended; record it and stop for the operator.

Task boundary: do only what the current task instruction lists and stop at its end, even when later steps of this brief remain; report the next step instead of performing it. Turn budget: if a task cannot finish, stop only with no runtime Form dirty and no prompt, list or dialog open, and report the next step.

Server-event rule (EXP-103-R2 lesson): if any action raises 'The server event processing returned an error', answer OK once, record it and stop blocked for an operator Designer reload; never try another route, retry, close or reopen after that error. Console-error stop (EXP-110-R2 lesson: a Caption commit can fail silently with HTTP 400 and surface only at the next server event): record the page console error count shown in the browser tool output at the start of each task and after every action in T1 to T3, for the tab in use (Web Client or Designer; record each tab's own baseline); if it rises after any action, record the action and the counts and stop blocked before any further click (no ellipsis, no Save, no close), leaving the state for the operator. Never read or inspect the console messages themselves. A rise can also come from a client-side Designer script error (EXP-111 T5: an uncaught TypeError at a component selection); the stop rule is the same, and the operator diagnoses the cause from the tool-written console log.

Gate (T1, read-only): list the tabs; identify the Web Client (portal app) and Web Designer tabs. In the Designer tab confirm User scope and that no open Form has unsaved changes (Save disabled); do not change it. In the Web Client record which runtime Form (if any) is open and whether it has unsaved changes; if a runtime Form has unsaved changes, record it and stop for the operator. Open the Web Client Form menu (view only), record whether its recent-forms list contains FX_CustomerPortal, and close the menu without choosing. Record each tab's baseline console error count and one screenshot of the Web Client with the menu open.

Efficiency rules (operator, 2026-10-16): screenshots only for the decisive states named in this brief; do not re-open saved images unless a decision needs it; one untargeted snapshot per step; read only the named sources; never search or read the worker's own session transcript. Use inline untargeted snapshots; never save snapshots to files and Grep them (EXP-109 ran out of turns that way). Lists (EXP-111 lesson): choose a list option by clicking it; never pick options with arrow keys, Enter or Tab while a list is open, because Tab commits the highlighted item. Stale references (operator ruling, EXP-111): the allowance is one fresh untargeted snapshot per 'Ref not found' error, not one per task. Snapshot size (EXP-114): if an untargeted snapshot is too large to return inline, take targeted snapshots of the needed panel instead (record that); never save snapshots to files.

Runtime open (T2): in the Web Client open FX_CustomerPortal once: through the Form menu recent-forms entry if it is listed (EXP-095 route); otherwise through the Web Client Open (Select Form) dialog by typing FX_CustomerPortal key by key in its filter and double-clicking the exact FX_CustomerPortal row (never OK; recipe create-basic-form.md). If neither route finds it, record it and stop blocked. Record the opened Form: title, status bar (record position text, mode), which regions and components are visible (header, menu buttons, sign-in page, home page with the Home heading and GridItems, buttons band, cart page, footer), what GridItems shows before any sign-in (empty, rows, tiles; how many), and any prompt verbatim (answer an OK-only informational prompt with OK; any other prompt: record it, choose No or Cancel and stop blocked). Do not type, filter, press F4 or click any button in T2. Screenshots: the opened Form; a closer view of the GridItems band if the first one does not show it clearly.

Sign-in check (T3): click into the Customer ID edit box (EditCustID, in the sign-in page under the Customer ID label) once and type 1 key by key; record the field value. Click the sign-in page's Sign In button (ButtonSignIn2, below the Customer ID edit; never the left menu's Sign In button) exactly once. Wait for the page to settle (at most 10 seconds), then record: any prompt or message verbatim (handle as in T2), the status bar, the console count, and what GridItems shows: tiles or rows, how many, and for each visible tile its picture (present or not, describe it), item, description and cost text. Scroll inside GridItems only with the mouse wheel and only to read further tiles (view only; record each scroll). Screenshots: after typing 1; after the click; the GridItems band showing the tiles. Then close the runtime Form once through the Web Client Form-close control; if a save prompt appears, record its text and answer No; record the state after the close. Then, in the same task, write the documentation-only final audit into the record: decisive evidence for each acceptance check, the cumulative action audit with exact counts, the worker-written-file inventory, the cleanup inventory (nothing created) and the final state.

Before every click, use references from the most recent snapshot taken in the current task (not from find output); after any timeout or 'Ref not found', take one fresh untargeted snapshot and use only its references (one per error). ExtJS comboboxes are not <select> elements (EXP-101): open their list and click the option. No coordinate clicks; if a control has no reference, record it and stop blocked. Record any blocker after at most one fresh untargeted snapshot and one corrected visible inspection; never leave a prompt, list, editor or dialog open across tasks. Classify findings as observed only.
